english: Make a vow to Father Sky!

plan.english: Make a vow to Father Sky!

notes: West 2007 ch. 4 names the case forms of Father Sky beyond the vocative: 'Homeric πατρὸς Διός, Διὶ πατρί; Italic … Iuve patre'; Schmitt 1967 §288 lists the eight Iguvine instances (IIa 5, 10; IIb 7, 17, 22, 24, 26; III 22). The line is that formula in the dative, as the god a vow or prayer is addressed to, which both branches attest with a verb or adjective of the root *h₁wegʷʰ- 'vow, pray solemnly'. Greek: εὐξάμενος/-οι Διὶ πατρί (Il. 17.498, Od. 13.51; Il. 16.253 the same after σπείσας), and Il. 24.287–288 σπεῖσον Διὶ πατρί, καὶ εὔχεο οἴκαδ' ἱκέσθαι (all checked in AGDT); there the dative is construed with σπεῖσον and εὔχεο takes the infinitive, so the passage is cited for the imperative of the prayer verb beside Διὶ πατρί, not for εὔχεο + dative. Umbrian (Buck 1904 OCR, checked; Tab. Ig. II is not in the UD treebank): in the offering of the votive calf, IIb 21–23 vitlu vufru … sestu Iuvepatre (Buck: 'vitulum votivum … sistito Iovi patri') and IIb 26 triiuper vufru naratu, fetu Iuvepatre ('ter votivum nuntiato, facito Iovi patri'); vufru 'votive' is the *-ro- adjective of *h₁wogʷʰ- (Buck §152 sets U. vufru, vufetes 'votis' beside L. voveō, Ved. vāghát- and Gk εὔχομαι). IIb 7 Afmune Iuve patre fetu writes the two words apart. Latin Cato Agr. 134.1 (LASLA, checked) has the dative of the god with a prayer verb (ture vino … Iovi … praefato) but not 'father', so it counts for *dyḗws only. Morphology: dative singular in both nouns, as in Διὶ πατρί and Iuve patre; Gk Διϝί has the zero grade *diw-éy of the engine, Umbr. Iuve the analogical full grade also seen in Lat. Iovī. Root-level only: the verb. Greek has the middle εὔχομαι, Umbrian the adjective vufru; the finite formation *h₁wogʷʰ-éye- is Latin voveō (Cato Agr. 83.1, a vow to Mars Silvanus, support) and is in neither parallel passage. Voice follows the attested cells, not the support ref: the only finite prayer verbs in the parallel passages are middle (Gk εὔχεο, εὐξάμενος) or deponent (Umbr. prepesnimu, support; Lat. precor, Cato Agr. 134.3 Iupiter … precor, checked in LASLA), so the line has the middle, though Latin voveō itself is active. Mood: 2sg imperative as in Il. 24.288 εὔχεο and the Umbrian ritual imperatives. Builder gaps: Umbr. Iuve and vufru are in no table (Buck §183 gives Iuve as the dat. sg. beside O. Diúvei, L. Iovī), and Iuvepatre reaches *dyḗws only through the compound. Same lexemes as sky-father-001/-003 (*dyéw ph₂ter): one evaluation group, though here the dative stands in both branches and the second branch is Italic.
